To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the boundary between the Jurassic Cosumnes Formation and the Logtown Ridge Formation should be redefined to remove all known paleontologic control from the Cosumnes; the type Cosumines Formation is now considered a part of the Calaveres megabreccias; the Cosumines is not a Jurassic unit; and rocks previously included in both the Amador Group and the Amador Formation are now included in the Calaveres Formation.

the type section of the Cosumne Formation should be moved downsection from the Cosumnes-Ryan Ranch Road bridge, that the type section is now located in the western belt of the Calaverias megabreccias, and that rocks in the type section of Cosumnes Formation could be older than Late Jurassic.

the Cosumnes Fm. and the Logtown Ridge Fm., which were originally considered to be conformable, are actually fault-bounded, and that the boundary between them should be relocated from its previous position at the Cosumne River to a location approximately 610 m down-section.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the geology of the type area of the Cosumines Formation and Logtown Ridge Formation, and the reinterpretation of the boundary between them.
the stratigraphy and tectonics of the Cosumne Formation and Logtown Ridge Formation.
the stratigraphic position, age, and origin of rocks that were formerly included in the Amador Group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Cosumnes is not the type of the Cosumines Formation, that the Logtown Ridge is not the type section of the Logtown Ridge Formation, that the Cosumines and Logtown Ridge are in fault contact, that the Cosumes Formation is a member of the Amador Group, and that the Cosumes is in fault contact with the Calaveras Group.
the type Cossumnes and Logtown formations are in fault contact.
the Cosumnes, Logtown Ridge, and western belt of the Calaverus Formations are not conformable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cosumnes, Logtown Ridge and Calaveras Formations are all Late Jurassic.
the Cosumnes “Formation” is not a formation, the Logtown Ridge “Formation” is probably a formation, the “western belt of the Calaveres” is not a belt, and the “Amador Group is not a group.
the Cosumnes “Formation” is a megabrecciated unit of rocks of uncertain age, and the Logtown Ridge “Formation” is the lower part of the Calavera Complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cosumnes formation should be considered to be a separate entity from the Amador group, and should not be used as a stratigraphic term for rocks in the Amador group.
the Cosumnes Fm. is not Jurassic, but is older.
the Jurassic Amador Formation is not present at its type locality and that the Jurassic age for the Logtown Ridge Formation is based on questionable data.
